title: Chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (India, HFAI)
subject: cardiology
setting: Outpatient clinic, cardiology, ward before discharge
summary: HFrEF is LVEF 40% or below. Start all four pillars (ARNI or ACEI/ARB, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2 inhibitor) at low dose as early as possible, preferably before discharge, and titrate to target or maximum tolerated doses within 4 to 6 weeks, using loop diuretics only for congestion.

sections.title: Diagnose and classify
items: Classify by LVEF on echo: HFrEF 40% or below; HFmrEF 41 to 49% (treated largely like HFrEF); HFpEF 50% or above; HF with improved EF: baseline 40% or below, a rise of 10 points or more and a second LVEF above 40%.
Specific signs: raised JVP, hepatojugular reflux, third heart sound, displaced apex. Look for congestion (orthopnoea, bendopnoea, oedema) and low output (cold peripheries).
Outpatients with breathlessness: BNP below 35 pg/mL or NT-proBNP below 125 pg/mL makes HF unlikely.

Acute presentation: rule out if BNP below 100 or NT-proBNP below 300 pg/mL. Rule in: BNP above 500, or NT-proBNP above 450 (under 50 years), above 900 (50 to 74 years), above 1800 pg/mL (75 years and over). ARNI raises BNP but not NT-proBNP; natriuretic peptides read low in obesity.

Coronary disease is the leading cause in India, followed by dilated cardiomyopathy and rheumatic heart disease: check troponin in acute HF and look for ischaemia, valve disease, alcohol, thyroid disease, tachycardia-induced and infiltrative cardiomyopathy.
Advanced HF clues: repeated admissions, NYHA III to IV despite therapy, refractory congestion, frequent systolic BP of 90 mmHg or below.

sections.title: The four pillars: start early, titrate fast
items: Give all four classes: ARNI (preferred) or ACEI/ARB, an evidence-based beta-blocker, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor. Even low doses help; adding a new class is worth more than up-titrating an existing one.

Sequencing in hospital: diuretics first for congestion; SGLT2 inhibitor and MRA early (little haemodynamic effect; SGLT2i needs no titration); beta-blocker before discharge once euvolaemic, off inotropes and without bradycardia; ACEI/ARB/ARNI before discharge if BP allows and no hyperkalaemia.
Up-titrate every 2 weeks, reaching target or maximum tolerated doses within 4 to 6 weeks (at most 3 months). At each visit check creatinine, electrolytes, BP including postural BP, and heart rate.

Beta-blocker targets: bisoprolol 1.25 mg to 10 mg once daily; carvedilol 3.125 mg to 25 mg twice daily; metoprolol succinate 12.5 to 25 mg to 200 mg once daily; nebivolol 1.25 mg to 10 mg once daily. Aim for resting heart rate below 70/min.
MRA: spironolactone 25 mg once daily or eplerenone 25 mg increasing to 50 mg once daily. SGLT2 inhibitor: dapagliflozin 10 mg or empagliflozin 10 mg once daily (starting and target dose).

ACEI/ARB start and target: enalapril 2.5 to 10 mg twice daily; ramipril 1.25 to 10 mg once daily; lisinopril 2.5 to 20 mg once daily; captopril 6.25 to 50 mg three times daily; candesartan 4 to 32 mg once daily; losartan 25 mg once daily to 50 mg twice daily; valsartan 40 to 160 mg twice daily.
Continue indefinitely even if EF improves: withdrawal after recovery led to relapse in 45%.

sections.title: Renal function, potassium and hypotension
items: A creatinine rise of up to 20% from baseline is not a reason to stop ACEI, ARB or ARNI. Be cautious as creatinine approaches 2 to 2.5 mg/dL; above 2.5 mg/dL, reduce or temporarily stop.
Potassium above 5 mEq/L: caution, especially with MRA; above 5.5 mEq/L: stop the MRA and review RAAS blockade.
For hypotension, first withdraw non-essential BP-lowering drugs (extra antihypertensives, excess diuretic) and NSAIDs rather than GDMT.

SGLT2 inhibitors: avoid if eGFR is below 20 mL/min/1.73 m2, in pregnancy and breastfeeding, or with hypotension; warn about genital fungal infection, dehydration and ketoacidosis; withhold around surgery.

Beta-blockers: avoid with second or third degree AV block, heart rate below 50/min, persisting congestion or hypotension, NYHA class IV or critical limb ischaemia; asthma is a relative contraindication.

sections.title: Diuretics and congestion
items: Loop diuretics relieve congestion but do not reduce mortality: use the lowest dose that keeps the patient euvolaemic, guided by daily weight.
In acute decompensation most patients need about twice their usual oral daily dose as IV loop diuretic, by bolus or infusion. About 400 to 600 mg IV furosemide a day is the ceiling.

Diuretic resistance: urine sodium not rising above 90 mEq/L despite more than 160 mg furosemide daily for 3 days. Options: switch diuretic, continuous infusion, add a thiazide, add an SGLT2 inhibitor or acetazolamide; tolvaptan or ultrafiltration only as rescue.
Needing escalation to very high oral diuretic doses without another cause should be treated as worsening HF.
Sodium 2 to 3 g a day is reasonable in India (down to 500 mg a day in severe HF); restrict fluids only in congested outpatients or symptomatic hyponatraemia, guided by thirst and weight.

sections.title: Beyond the four pillars
items: Iron deficiency (ferritin below 100 microgram/L, or 100 to 300 with transferrin saturation below 20%): IV ferric carboxymaltose 500 to 1000 mg in 50 mL saline over 10 to 15 minutes; recheck iron after 2 to 3 months and repeat if still low. Oral iron is not advised.

Vericiguat after an HF hospitalisation or outpatient IV diuretic need, with EF below 45%: 2.5 mg once daily, doubling about every 2 weeks to 10 mg once daily. Not with PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil) or riociguat.

Ivabradine: LVEF below 35%, sinus rhythm and heart rate above 70/min despite maximally tolerated beta-blocker, or to allow beta-blocker titration when BP is low. Not in pregnancy or with CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, macrolides).
Digoxin: symptomatic patients in sinus rhythm despite GDMT (reduces admissions, not deaths) or AF rate control when other options fail; keep level 0.5 to 0.9 ng/mL; caution in the elderly and CKD.

Hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate if ACEI, ARB and ARNI are not tolerated: fixed combination isosorbide dinitrate 20 mg with hydralazine 37.5 mg three times daily, up to 40 mg with 75 mg three times daily.
Anticoagulate HF with AF (a NOAC unless there is a mechanical valve); no anticoagulation without an indication. Continue statins and antiplatelets when CAD is present.

sections.title: Devices and referral
items: ICD for primary prevention if LVEF remains 35% or below after at least 3 months of optimised therapy; for secondary prevention after VF or haemodynamically unstable VT without a reversible cause.
CRT for symptomatic patients in sinus rhythm with LVEF 35% or below and LBBB with QRS 130 ms or more; consider if non-LBBB with QRS 150 ms or more.
Refer for advanced HF assessment (mechanical support, transplant) when advanced features persist despite optimised GDMT.
Device use in Indian registries is below 2% although about half of deaths are sudden: actively screen eligible patients.

sections.title: Discharge and follow-up
items: Discharge when precipitants are treated, near-euvolaemic on oral diuretics, stable renal function and electrolytes, no symptomatic hypotension, and oral regimen stable for at least 24 hours with GDMT started.

Educate on medicines, salt, daily weights, graded activity and when to seek help. Clinic review within 7 days of discharge, then every 1 to 2 weeks while titrating; the first 3 months carry the highest risk of readmission and death.
At each visit review symptoms, congestion, weight, heart rate, BP (including postural), potassium, eGFR and NT-proBNP.
Vaccinate: pneumococcal (conjugate and PPSV23) and annual influenza. Recommend regular aerobic exercise and cardiac rehabilitation.

sections.title: Pregnancy and CKD
items: Pregnancy: ACEI, ARB, ARNI, MRA and SGLT2 inhibitors are contraindicated; metoprolol is the preferred beta-blocker; digoxin and diuretics can be used. Use LMWH (first and last trimester) or VKA/LMWH (second trimester) if anticoagulation is needed; avoid DOACs.
Breastfeeding: captopril, enalapril, spironolactone, beta-blockers and digoxin are compatible; avoid SGLT2 inhibitors.
CKD: ARNI shows slower eGFR decline and less hyperkalaemia than ACEI or ARB (studied down to eGFR 30); SGLT2 inhibitors studied down to eGFR 20; higher diuretic doses are often needed.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Waiting to reach target doses of one drug before starting the next class.
Stopping RAAS blockers for a small creatinine rise, or MRA for potassium below 5.5 mEq/L.
Starting a beta-blocker in a congested or hypotensive patient.
Discharging on high diuretics without GDMT and without review within 7 days.
Reading a raised BNP on ARNI as worsening HF (use NT-proBNP).

drugs.name: Bisoprolol
drugs.dose: Start 1.25 mg once daily; target 10 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Start when euvolaemic; titrate every 2 weeks.

drugs.name: Carvedilol
drugs.dose: Start 3.125 mg twice daily; target 25 mg twice daily
drugs.notes: Start when euvolaemic; titrate every 2 weeks.

drugs.name: Metoprolol succinate (CR/XL)
drugs.dose: Start 12.5 to 25 mg once daily; target 200 mg once daily

drugs.name: Eplerenone
drugs.dose: Start 25 mg once daily; target 50 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Check potassium and creatinine at each titration.

drugs.name: Dapagliflozin or empagliflozin
drugs.dose: 10 mg orally once daily (start and target)
drugs.notes: Avoid if eGFR below 20; withhold peri-operatively.

drugs.name: Enalapril
drugs.dose: Start 2.5 mg twice daily; target 10 mg twice daily

drugs.name: Ramipril
drugs.dose: Start 1.25 mg once daily; target 10 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Alternative to ARNI; check creatinine and potassium.

drugs.name: Vericiguat
drugs.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, then 5 mg, then 10 mg once daily at about 2-week steps
drugs.notes: Worsening HF with EF below 45%. Not with PDE5 inhibitors.

drugs.name: Ferric carboxymaltose
drugs.dose: 500 to 1000 mg IV in 50 mL saline over 10 to 15 minutes
drugs.notes: Iron deficiency; reassess at 2 to 3 months.

sources.title: 2025 HFAI guidelines for diagnosis and management of heart failure (Heart Fail J India 2025;3 Suppl 1:S1-48)
